author: Benjamin George Sports Editor
title: Lincoln's Tate, Notre Dame's McIntyre reflect at end of state tournament | West Virginia High School Sports | wvnews.com
text:
WHEELING, W. Va. — The second day of the Class AA/A tournament at the WVSSAC State Golf Tournament has concluded, and the final champions of the 2026 golf season have been crowned.
Class A was won by Wirt County freshman Jude Walker with 154 total strokes (par), while St. Marys’ Trevor Maley placed second at 159 strokes and Richwood’s Weston Wayne in third with 162.
Wirt County also took the team state title at 493 total strokes, 15 less than second place St. Marys and 46 less than third place Charleston Catholic. The title is Wirt County’s second and first since 2002, while Walker gives the Tigers their first individual champion in school history and the first freshman winner in any class since Washington’s Tommy Evans in 2023.
Class AA saw Midland Trail take both team and individual titles as well, meaning the Patriots have gone back-to-back in both team and individual titles. This marks the first such feat since Jacob Brown and Wheeling Park accomplished it in 2010 and 2011.
The Patriots shot 476 as a team, while Wheeling Central took second at 497 and Wyoming East placed third with 505. Jacob Brown took his 2nd straight title with 150 strokes, Berkeley Spring’s Cayden Swink finished second at 158 ahead of a tie for 3rd at 159 between Brown’s teammate Camryn Thomas andWeir’s Guy Meneely.
Lincoln’s Nick Tate and Notre Dame’s Colton McIntyre finished their seasons off after breaking tournament appearance droughts for the respective schools, Lincoln’s last showing at Oglebay being in 2022 and Notre Dame in 2021. Tate finished his high school career at 27th in Class AA, and McIntyre his junior year at 36th for A.
For McIntyre, the appearance represents the fruits of hard work, a notion supported by his head coach Katie Gallagher.
“He worked hard in the offseason, fought to get here, he literally went against one other player to come here, and I’m extremely proud of him,” said Gallagher after McIntyre had completed the round.
“He’s the first player that I’ve had as head coach to make it to states, so that’s pretty awesome. I know he’s not done or satisfied, and he’s not happy with his performance. But that just shows me he wants to keep getting better, and I’m extremely proud of him for battling back. Our goal was to get here, and that’s what we did, and we’ll be back next year.”
McIntyre spoke on his performance as well.
“I had some trouble, but still came here and made it, so I can’t be mad. It’s a very, very demanding course, especially physically. You have to come out all 18 holes with a level head, and today just wasn’t there, but we’ll work on that. I can’t be mad at how I performed, it is what it is.
“Even going back to that regional playoff, sinking that putt and him missing it, that was probably one of the greatest feelings that I’ve ever felt. It’s a memory I will never forget. I also got out of school and missed a religion test; sorry, but we made it.”
Tate’s performance presents the last golf he will play as a member of the Cougars, finishing off a run that head coach Josh Leep saw as an excellent ending for a player he has coached for all four years.
“My whole coaching career, he’s been on my team; his first day was my first day,” reflected Leep. “He had a couple of rough holes, didn’t get his head down or panic and refocused, and played a lot better on the back 9.
“Great kid, great competitor, always wants to get better and a great leader for the younger kids. I’m definitely going to miss him. I think with Nick making it, the rest of the guys realize that if they can step up and do the same thing. I’m hoping next year we can get a whole team up here. If not, we’ll do the best we can to have a repeat just like Nick had.”
Tate gave a final reflection following the completion of his round. “I’d say I did all right, definitely had a couple bad holes but I recovered pretty decent, and it feels pretty good to break the drought. I’m a little bit sad, but golf’s a sport I can play for the rest of my life.”

Tate finished his high school career at 27th in Class AA, and McIntyre his junior year at 36th for A. For McIntyre, the appearance represents the fruits of hard work, a notion supported by his head coach Katie Gallagher.
